meta.title: Session log upload
meta.description: Chooses when Session logs are uploaded to DeepSeek's official API or to a destination you set: never, only the official API, any provider's DeepSeek models, or any model.

upload.sectionDescription: A Session log is the durable record of one conversation: your messages, model output, tool results, and the file paths involved. This setting decides when DSH sends that record to the destination below.
upload.modeUnknown: The Host has not reported the current mode.

off.label: Never upload
off.detail: Nothing is sent, and DSH's built-in official-API upload is switched off too.

officialOnly.label: Only the official DeepSeek API
officialOnly.detail: DSH's built-in behaviour. The log rides along with requests that were already going to DeepSeek.

deepseekAnyProvider.label: Any provider's DeepSeek models
deepseekAnyProvider.detail: Also uploads when a DeepSeek model is served by a different provider.

anyModel.label: Any model
anyModel.detail: Uploads after every model request, whichever provider answered it.

upload.warnTitle: Send this Session log to the destination below?
upload.warnBody: The log is sent to the destination below. That includes your messages, tool output, file paths, and conversations you held with other model providers. It leaves this machine, it may be used to improve and train models, and it cannot be undone.
upload.patternsHelp: Matched against the model id, ignoring case. Add a name here if a provider serves DeepSeek under a different one, such as dfmodel.
upload.patternsEmpty: Nothing added yet. Only the default deepseek pattern is used.
upload.directoriesLabel: Never upload sessions from these folders
upload.directoriesHelp: One path per line. Sessions in these folders or their subfolders are not uploaded. DSH’s own official upload is stopped for them too.
upload.endpointInvalid: Not saved: the destination must be an http:// or https:// address.
upload.capInvalid: Not saved: the byte cap must be a whole number of bytes, 1 or more.

ledger.title: Uploaded Sessions
ledger.description: An index of the Session logs this plugin has uploaded: session id, how far each was uploaded, when, and the format version. It does not contain the log content itself.
ledger.titlesDetail: A session name comes from the conversation itself, so turning this on shows a slice of its content on this page. Off by default; the detailed log is otherwise metadata only.
ledger.columnsHint: “Uploaded through” is the sequence number of the last session event this plugin has sent for that session; session events are numbered as the conversation grows. “Format version” identifies the session-log format generation, so a format change makes the plugin resend rather than mix incompatible records.
ledger.skipped: Records without a session id were skipped:
ledger.empty: Nothing recorded yet. This detailed log covers uploads made by this plugin only: in “Never upload” or “Only the official DeepSeek API” mode it stays empty by design, and uploads made by DSH's built-in official-API uploader are never listed here.
ledger.stateMissing: The Host does not serve the detailed log at this address, so there is nothing to show.
ledger.stateUnauthorized: The request was refused: this page is not authorized to read the detailed log.
ledger.stateMalformed: The Host answered, but the detailed log could not be read.
ledger.stateFailed: The detailed log could not be read.
ledger.failureUnreported: The Host did not report the last upload failure, so this page cannot say whether an upload is failing.
ledger.failureNone: No upload failure has been recorded.
ledger.failureRetryable: This failure is retried automatically, but nothing has been delivered yet.
ledger.failureNotRetryable: This failure is not retried automatically.
ledger.failurePersistent: This is not a one-off: the same problem has repeated.
ledger.failureUnresolved: This will not clear on its own: until the byte cap changes, every upload stays too large.
ledger.failureKindNoCredential: No usable API credential was found for the upload.
ledger.failureKindEndpointRefused: The destination is not a usable http:// or https:// address, so nothing was sent.
ledger.failureKindHttpError: The destination answered with an error.
ledger.failureKindTransportError: The request could not reach the destination (network or DNS).
ledger.failureKindPayloadTooLarge: The log is larger than the byte cap, so it was not sent.
ledger.failureKindUnknown: The Host reported a failure it could not classify.

upload.saveFailed: The setting could not be saved.
upload.manualHint: This browser could not write the setting. Add the configuration below to cordis.patch.yml, or run the command in a Session.
upload.renderFailed: This settings section could not be rendered.
